rows.sentence: The article in the document is about tirzepatide, which it describes as "The diabetes and weight loss drug tirzepatide (Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes; Zepbound for obesity)."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article identifies tirzepatide as a diabetes and weight-loss drug and specifies the uses of the two brand names.

rows.sentence: Mechanistically, the document identifies it as "a long-acting glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonist and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article explicitly identifies tirzepatide as an agonist of both receptors.

rows.sentence: **The connection to sleep apnea.**
rows.label: no_rad
rows.rationale: This is a section heading, not a factual assertion.

rows.sentence: The link the document draws between tirzepatide and sleep apnea runs through obesity.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article presents obesity as a risk factor for OSA and explains why an obesity treatment is relevant to OSA care, without establishing a mechanism.

rows.sentence: It states that "Obesity is a common risk factor" for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), and that "40% of those with obesity have OSA and 70% of those with OSA have obesity."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article explicitly identifies the risk factor and gives both percentages.

rows.sentence: Because the drug treats obesity, it was tested in OSA patients: the "SURMOUNT-OSA studies" were "two double-blind randomized controlled trials in patients with obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA" conducted "at 60 sites in nine countries," with results "presented here at the American Diabetes Association (ADA) 84th Scientific Sessions and simultaneously published online in the New England Journal of Medicine."
rows.label: unsupported
rows.rationale: The article confirms the trial design, locations, presentation, and publication, but does not explicitly establish that treating obesity was the reason the investigators tested the drug in OSA patients.

rows.sentence: In the trials, patients were enrolled "who had moderate-to-severe OSA, defined as more than 15 events per hour (using the apnea–hypopnea index [AHI]) and a body mass index of 30 kg/m2 or greater."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article specifies both the AHI and BMI enrollment thresholds.

rows.sentence: Those not using a CPAP device were in study 1, and those using one were in study 2.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article explicitly distinguishes the two study populations by CPAP use.

rows.sentence: Participants "received either the maximum tolerated dose of tirzepatide (10 or 15 mg by once-weekly injection) or placebo for 1 year," along with lifestyle counseling.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article gives the dosing schedule and duration and says all participants received lifestyle counseling.

rows.sentence: **Results.**
rows.label: no_rad
rows.rationale: This is a section heading, not a factual assertion.

rows.sentence: The drug produced a large reduction in apnea events.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The reported reduction in events per hour was substantially larger with tirzepatide than with placebo.

rows.sentence: "By 1 year, patients taking tirzepatide had 27 to 30 fewer events/hour compared with 4 to 6 fewer events/hour for those taking placebo."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article gives these exact one-year results for tirzepatide and placebo.

rows.sentence: "Up to half of those who received tirzepatide in both trials had less than 5 events/hour or 5 to 14 AHI events/hour and an Epworth Sleepiness Scale score of 10 or less," thresholds that "represent a level at which CPAP therapy may not be recommended."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article reports those thresholds and explicitly says that CPAP may not be recommended at that level.

rows.sentence: Overall, the drug "was so effective at reducing sleep disruptions in patients with obesity and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) that 40% to 50% no longer needed to use a continuous pressure airway positive (CPAP) device."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article's opening paragraph explicitly makes this claim and gives the same percentage range.

rows.sentence: Weight loss: "patients taking the medication lost 18% to 20% of their body weight."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article reports the same range of body-weight loss.

rows.sentence: Blood pressure and inflammation: tirzepatide "also lowered C-reactive protein levels and systolic blood pressure," with "a decrease in systolic blood pressure from baseline of 9.7 mm Hg in study 1 and 7.6 mm Hg in study 2 at Week 48."
rows.label: unsupported
rows.rationale: The article supports the reported measurements, but it does not identify the reduction in C-reactive protein as an inflammation benefit.

rows.sentence: In an accompanying editorial, Sanjay R. Patel wrote that this improvement "was substantially larger than effects seen with CPAP therapy alone and indicate that tirzepatide may be an attractive option for those patients who seek to reduce their cardiovascular risk."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article attributes both the blood-pressure comparison and the potential cardiovascular relevance to Patel's editorial.

rows.sentence: Sleep-related quality of life: "Patients who received tirzepatide also reported fewer daytime and nighttime disturbances, as measured using the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Short Form scale for Sleep-Related Impairment and Sleep Disturbance."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article reports fewer patient-reported daytime and nighttime disturbances and names the instrument used to measure them.

rows.sentence: An alternative to CPAP: "CPAP is an effective and the most-used intervention for OSA, but many patients refuse to use the device, stop using it, or cannot use it," and "This new drug treatment offers a more accessible alternative for individuals who cannot tolerate or adhere to existing therapies."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article describes the barriers to CPAP use and quotes Malhotra presenting tirzepatide as a more accessible alternative for some patients.

rows.sentence: Should tirzepatide "eventually gain US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for OSA, it would be the first drug approved for the condition."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article explicitly makes this conditional claim about FDA approval.

rows.sentence: **Cautions the document raises.**
rows.label: no_rad
rows.rationale: This is a section heading, not a factual assertion.

rows.sentence: "The most common adverse events were diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting, which occurred in approximately a quarter of patients taking tirzepatide.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article lists these as the most common adverse events and gives the same approximate frequency.

rows.sentence: There were two adjudicated-confirmed cases of acute pancreatitis in those taking tirzepatide in study 2."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article reports exactly two confirmed acute pancreatitis cases in the tirzepatide group in study 2.

rows.sentence: Patel "raised concerns about whether patients outside of a trial would stick with therapy, noting studies have shown high rates of discontinuation of GLP-1 receptor agonists," and raised concerns about "Racial disparities in the use of GLP-1 receptor agonists among patients with diabetes."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article attributes both the adherence concern and the concern about racial disparities to Patel.

rows.sentence: Finally, Louis Aronne noted that "It is still not clear whether tirzepatide had an independent effect in the OSA trial — as has been seen in other studies where the drug clearly reduced cardiovascular risk — or whether the positive results were primarily due to weight loss," adding, "I believe that over time we'll see that this particular effect in sleep apnea is related to weight."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article reports both Aronne's uncertainty about the cause of the improvement and his belief that the effect is related to weight.

rows.sentence: He also said the trials demonstrate "the treatment of obesity with tirzepatide plus CPAP is really the optimal treatment for obstructive sleep apnea and obesity-related cardiometabolic risks."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article attributes this interpretation of the trial results to Aronne.

rows.sentence: Regarding your own situation: the document does not state whether tirzepatide would help you personally.
rows.label: no_rad
rows.rationale: This is a disclaimer that avoids making a personalized prediction.

rows.sentence: The trials enrolled patients with obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA (AHI greater than 15 and BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater), and the document does not address how the results would apply to any individual patient outside those criteria.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The article specifies those eligibility thresholds and reports results for the enrolled population without discussing individual outcomes outside it.
